summary: Gustaf John Ramstedt specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1902) and later held posts there (~1901–1941) and at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

A sinologist, Gustav Haloun studied at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Charles University. He held positions at Halle, Göttingen (1931–1938), and served as Chair of Chinese Language and History at the University of Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, Göttingen, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto (~1920–1924), later holding academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle, Munich, and Patna under teachers including Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn, Leipzig University, Halle-Wittenberg, and the Berlin University of the Arts, where he also held a post.

Gustave Lanson studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held teaching posts at Lycée Charlemagne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the Faculty of Arts of Paris/University of Paris (~1900–1927), and Columbia University (~1911–1912).
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He has held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Religious studies scholar Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Paris, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, EPHE, and Harvard. He held positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1978 to 2009 and served as professor at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and studied under teachers including Donald S. Lopez Jr., later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Patrul Rinpoche.
Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He served as Acting Director (1972) and Director (1974–1998) of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He held posts at Taisho University as president (~1926–1944), the University of Tokyo as professor (1928), and Toyo University as a lecturer.

Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004) and as a researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978). He also held academic posts at Rissho University as an assistant professor (~1984–1993) and professor (~1993).
Gyomay Kubose was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu from ~1937 to 1941.
Gyosho Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged between 1928 and 1934 and held a post at Nyugat.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gyurme Dorje studied at Edinburgh and SOAS under Philip T. Denwood. He was a research fellow at SOAS/University of London (1991–1996) and a translator for the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok was a scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
